title: Qcqs matching scheme for the next finite degree
statement: For a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme X and a truncated finite split etale hypercover U through n [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover], there exist boundary data [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-replacement-stage] for degree n+1, universal among all schemes over X, with quasi-compact quasi-separated matching scheme.

source.place: 0DAV, next matching object as a finite limit; original replacement proof step 1, qcqs finite limits.

proof.text: Map each finite coproduct cofan for N_q into schemes. The colimit point is isomorphic to a finite coproduct of its qcqs pieces, whose topology is their finite disjoint union. Compactness follows from finiteness; for quasi-separatedness, pull compact opens back to each clopen component, intersect there, and take the finite union of the compact images. Apply the same argument to the splitting cofan to deduce that every term of U is qcqs.

Use the morphism property P consisting of etale, quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphisms. It is multiplicative and stable under base change. It permits cancellation of postcomposition by P: etaleness cancels along etale maps, quasi-compactness cancels along quasi-separated maps, and quasi-separatedness cancels without a condition. Therefore P.Over X has finite limits and its inclusion into Over X preserves them. Every term of U lifts to P.Over X by the preceding step and qcqs permanence.

The category of maps from retained simplices to [n+1] has finitely many objects and arrows. Take the opposite boundary diagram in P.Over X and form its limit. Regard its point as an etale X-scheme M. The limit projections give all boundary projections; the cone equations give naturality. Preservation of the finite limit into Over X gives the required universal property for arbitrary schemes over X.
The structure map of the limit belongs to P. Its quasi-compactness and the compactness of X imply compactness of M. Its quasi-separatedness and that of X imply quasi-separatedness of M.
